issue.title: [bug] read_file truncation reports characters, so the agent cannot compute where to continue
issue.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I can reproduce this on the latest `main`.

### Problem summary

`read_file` head-truncates at a character offset and tells the model to continue with `start_line`/`end_line`, but reports only character counts, so the model has no way to know which line the cut fell on.

### Affected area(s)

Agents / LangGraph (graph, prompts, langgraph.json); Sandbox / Docker

### What happened?

`read_file` output above `sandbox.read_file_output_max_chars` (default 50,000) is head-truncated by `_truncate_read_file_output` (`backend/packages/harness/deerflow/sandbox/tools.py:1843`), which appends:

```
... [truncated: showing first 49892 of 111577 chars. Use start_line/end_line to read a specific range] ...
```

The marker asks for a line-based continuation but gives a character position. The cut is made at a character offset, so it almost always lands in the middle of a line, and `read_file` returns raw text without line numbers, so nothing in the result says which line that was.

Reading this repository's own `backend/packages/harness/deerflow/sandbox/tools.py` at `f7f4a022` (111,577 chars, 2,671 lines) with the default limit:

- the output is cut after 49,892 chars, inside line 1238, keeping 32 of that line's 59 chars
- the last line the model sees, `    single identifier placeholde`, is a fragment that reads as a complete line
- to continue without a gap the model has to send `start_line=1238`; nothing in the result implies 1238

The same happens on prose. At the same limit:

| file at `f7f4a022` | size | where the cut lands |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | 155,704 chars, 1,828 lines | inside line 745, keeping 16 of 85 chars (`2. Set the messa`) |
| `backend/docs/CONFIGURATION.md` | 67,244 chars, 1,203 lines | inside line 910, keeping 219 of 480 chars |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | 173,671 chars, 2,871 lines | inside line 782, keeping 49 of 81 chars |

6 of the repository's 236 Markdown files and 74 of its 1,531 Python files are over the limit.

#### What models do with the current marker

A small probe, not an evaluation: the truncated `README.md` result (the copy at `14c9d444`, 155,679 chars, 1,830 lines, cut inside line 745 as above) was handed to a model as the output of `read_file(path)`, with a task whose answer sits at line 1506, and the model was asked for the JSON arguments of its next `read_file` call. Five samples per marker per model, no temperature or reasoning settings sent (provider defaults). Correct continuation: `start_line=745`.

| model | marker | `start_line` in 5 samples | exact | what `read_file` then does | mean output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek V4 Pro (`deepseek-v4-pro`, official API) | current | 500, 700, 700, 700, 1300 | 0/5 | 4× overlap (45–245 lines re-read), 1× gap (lines 745–1299 never read) | 1463 |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro | proposed | 745 ×5 | 5/5 | exact continuation | 469 |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (`deepseek-flash`, official API) | current | 900, 700, 1500, 900, 500 | 0/5 | 3× gap (155–755 lines skipped), 2× overlap | 276 |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | proposed | 745 ×5 | 5/5 | exact continuation | 141 |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B (local Ollama, thinking on) | current | 50000, 50000, 1, 1500, 50000 | 0/5 | 3× `(start_line exceeds file length)`, 1× re-read from the top and truncated identically, 1× gap | 1011 |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B | proposed | 745 ×5 | 5/5 | exact continuation | 134 |

Across 15 samples with the current marker no model landed on the right line: the DeepSeek models estimate a round number from the character count and land 45–245 lines early or 155–755 lines late; the smaller model takes the character count for a line number. With the proposed marker all 15 samples are exact, and output tokens drop two- to threefold because there is nothing left to reason about. Script and raw responses are attached.

### Expected behavior

The marker tells the model, in the units its continuation parameters use, exactly where the shown text ends and where to continue, and the cut does not leave a partial line that looks complete.

### Steps to reproduce

No agent or model needed; the function is pure:

```bash
cd backend && PYTHONPATH=packages/harness uv run python - <<'PY'
from deerflow.sandbox.tools import _truncate_read_file_output

content = open("packages/harness/deerflow/sandbox/tools.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
out = _truncate_read_file_output(content, 50_000)
kept = out.index("\n... [truncated:")
print(content[:kept].count("\n") + 1)   # 1238: the line the cut fell inside
print(repr(out[kept - 60:kept]))        # a mid-line fragment
print(repr(out[kept:]))                 # the marker: characters only
PY
```

### Relevant logs

```
... [truncated: showing first 49892 of 111577 chars. Use start_line/end_line to read a specific range] ...
```

### How are you running DeerFlow?

Local (make dev)

### Platform details

macOS 26 (Apple Silicon), Python 3.12, `main` at `f7f4a022`

---

### Why it matters for documents

Uploaded PDFs are converted to Markdown by pymupdf4llm (MarkItDown as fallback) and Office files by MarkItDown, then read with `read_file`. At roughly 3,000 chars per page of English prose, the default limit is about 16 pages, and Markdown tables from reports and spreadsheets push a file over it sooner. A twenty-page contract or report is cut, and the section the user asked about is usually past the cut.

### Why it is worth fixing

- Recovering from the cut is exactly what the marker asks for, and the result carries no information that makes it possible. The model can only estimate a line from a character count, re-read overlapping ranges, or spend a `bash` call on `wc -l` / `grep -n`; each is another model call over the full context.
- A silently cut last line can be taken for real content. DeerFlow edits with `str_replace`, which matches context text, so a fragment copied into `old_string` fails to match or matches the wrong place.
- #3377 externalizes oversized tool outputs and its synopsis says "Use read_file on … with start_line and end_line to inspect the raw output", and `read_file` is in `tool_output.exempt_tools` by default, so those read-backs go through this same character-based path.

### Proposal

Two small changes inside the truncation branch of `_truncate_read_file_output`; the read output format itself does not change, and reads under the limit stay byte-identical because the early return at the top of the function is untouched.

1. Cut at the last line boundary before the limit instead of mid-line (fall back to the character cut only when the kept span has no newline).
2. Report the position in lines, name the next read explicitly, and keep the character counts:

```
... [truncated: showing first 1237 of 2671 lines (49860 of 111577 chars). Continue with start_line=1238, or use start_line/end_line to read a specific range] ...
```

Cost: the marker grows from 29 to 46 tokens (o200k) per truncated read, and a truncated read is about 11,400 tokens, so the marker is a rounding error; one avoided locate-and-retry turn saves far more. `tests/test_tool_output_truncation.py` pins the under-limit passthrough today; its marker-format assertions would be updated with the marker. Nothing else in the backend or the frontend parses the marker text.

A larger alternative would be line-numbered `read_file` output paged by lines. It solves the same problem more thoroughly but changes every read's format and costs tokens on every line, so I am not proposing it here.

### Fix

Implemented in #5474: the cut lands on a line boundary and the marker names the next `start_line`, with regression tests. If you want behavioral evidence beyond the unit tests and the probe above, tell me what would convince you and I will produce it.

steps: Create /mnt/user-data/workspace/long.txt with 4000 numbered lines using Python, each line formatted as line-00001 followed by 80 x characters, incrementing the number. Read it with read_file and follow the tool continuation guidance to read the remaining lines.
expected: A truncated read provides a source-line continuation position and does not present a cut fragment as a complete line.
defect: read_file clips the rendered text at a character limit and reports character counts without a usable next source line.
